name: atmosphere
description: The atmosphere of music refers to the familiar sensations and images which are conveyed to the listener. Atmosphere is distinguished from mood in that the latter is largely associated with emotions, not imagery.

name: apocalyptic
description: Music which evokes imagery of the end of the world or catastrophic destruction.

name: bright
description: Music with a bright atmosphere evokes imagery full of light or liveliness. Brightness that is imagined as full of light can come from various sources of light found in reality, such as fire, heat, or luminescent objects. Brightness that is imagined as full of life refers to a sensation of vividness that typically bears some relation to the perceived mood of the music. Brightness in music can also refer to the sound quality of an instrument or voice. Brightness in this sense refers to a clear and strong high-frequency sound. Certain instruments, such as the trumpet, naturally produce bright timbres, but the modes utilized within music can help reinforce a bright sound; generally speaking, in Western music theory, major scales carry a brighter sound, whereas minor scales are the opposite, bearing darker sonic qualities. The tonal quality of an instrument also depends on the recording and/or production of the music being played. A bright atmosphere can be brought about by any of these definitions, if not all at once.

name: cavernous
description: Cavernous music evokes the depths of caverns or of similarly large inner spaces, typically through an emphasis on lower frequencies or the presence of reverb or echo, whether due to the recording location or as a result of techniques used during production.

name: cold
description: A cold atmosphere evokes the sensation of low temperatures or lack of physical warmth, such as bitter weather, freezing environments, or other such landscapes. It may be brought about by or related to frosty tones.

name: cozy
description: Cozy music evokes sensations of comfort, safety, and intimacy as well as typically evoking sensations of warmth and softness.

name: dark
description: Dark music evokes imagery that is infernal, mysterious, ominous, or gloomy.

name: funereal
description: Music with a funereal atmosphere evokes imagery of mourning and sorrow, and is often paired with a sombre mood.

name: gothic
description: Music with a gothic atmosphere evokes gloomy sensations and images, often mixed with grotesque or supernatural elements, drawing on the influence of Gothic literature, art, and architecture. The term Gothic was originally used to describe the architecture of late medieval Europe but later became associated with the goth subculture and its particular styles of music. More generally, the term is used to apply to music with a gloomy atmosphere influenced by popular perceptions of Gothic architecture as well as the literature of the 18th and 19th century, which is commonly referred to as Gothic and dark romanticism. A gothic atmosphere is common in, though not limited to, Gothic Rock. It also is frequently found in genres such as Metal, Darkwave, Gothic Country, and Neofolk.

name: infernal
description: Music which evokes the imagery of hell, fire, demons, death, and/or torment.

name: ominous
description: An ominous atmosphere evokes a sense that something evil, unfortunate, or unpleasant will happen. It is typically perceived as an outcome that cannot be avoided or as a warning must be heeded at all costs; either way, such a sensation consequently makes the listener feel powerless in their situation. Because believing in an omen can be superstitious, there is sometimes a supernatural aura surrounding an ominous atmosphere.

name: daytime
description: A daytime atmosphere evokes imagery of the time between sunrise and sunset, such as bright sunlight, clear skies, and gentle warmth. It may be brought about by or related to radiant tones.

name: epic
description: Epic music is grand in scale, often very long and ambitious, focusing on narratives framed with great significance, inviting comparison to epic poetry. Themes and events common in epic poetry are also often incorporated or referenced, including heroes, wars, adventures, fantastical events, mythology, and moral lessons.

name: ethereal
description: Music which evokes heavenly, airy, elegant, and/or graceful imagery.

name: futuristic
description: Music with a futuristic atmosphere evokes the imagery of a time yet to come, especially advanced technology and other elements often seen in science fiction.

name: hazy
description: Music that evokes imagery obscured by some atmospheric covering. Natural haze occurs from aerosols, which includes water (i.e., fog, mist, vapor), dust, or smoke; however, haziness does not have to come strictly from natural sources. Although this descriptor can refer to real-world landscapes in which visibility is low, often a hazy atmosphere relates to the inability to distinguish visions within the mind, especially distant memories. Because of this attribute, hazy atmospheres can be very moody and may have an overlap with other atmospheres, particularly surreal, ethereal, psychedelic, and mysterious.

name: hypnotic
description: Hypnotic music evokes the imagery or feelings of hypnosis, such as a higher response toward suggestions and a decrease in general awareness. It's also often repetitive in nature.

name: martial
description: Music which evokes the imagery of armed forces, wars and military bands.

name: mechanical
description: Music which evokes the imagery of machinery or industrial scenery.

name: medieval
description: Music which evokes the Middle Ages era, which started in the fifth century and ended in the early fifteenth century in Europe.

name: mysterious
description: Music which evokes a sense of mystery. It generally conveys that there is something that the listener should know or understand, but which eludes them. The source of the mystery does not need to be something that can be defined, as in an unanswered question posed by the lyrics - rather, it's enough for there to be a general sense of mystery about the music.

name: natural
description: Music which evokes the imagery of the natural environment. This is achieved through the heavy use of real Nature Recordings/Field Recording, the use of electronics and acoustics to imitate the real sounds, or a combination of both.

name: aquatic
description: Music which evokes imagery of water landscapes or oceans through ambient or atmospheric effect, and/or the use of Field Recording.

name: desert
description: Music with a desert atmosphere evokes imagery of a type of arid land with sparse vegetation that is typically characterized by sandy terrain and a hot climate, although certain deserts (such as polar deserts) are icy and cold.

name: forest
description: Music with a forest atmosphere evokes imagery of large areas of land that are densely populated by trees and other vegetation. These areas typically have diverse plant and animal ecosystems.

name: grassland
description: Music with a grassland atmosphere evokes imagery of great expanses of flat or gently undulating terrain covered predominantly by grasses, with moderate but inconsistent rainfall and sharp seasonal contrasts.

name: mountains
description: Music with an atmosphere of mountains evokes the imagery of cliffs, crags, rocky or snowy peaks, vast ranges, and sparse highland or alpine terrain.

name: rain
description: Music which evokes the imagery of rain.

name: storm
description: Music which evokes the imagery of storms, characterized by torrential rain, howling winds, heavy snowfall, dark clouds, and rolling thunder, often through Field Recording.

name: tropical
description: Music which evokes the imagery of the tropics, a region often associated with beaches, lush vegetation, and exotic wildlife.

name: wetland
description: Music with a wetland atmosphere evokes imagery of semiaquatic environments with oxygen-poor soil usually saturated or flooded with water, which act as transitional zones between land and bodies of water.

name: wind
description: Music with an atmosphere of wind evokes the sensations and images of windswept terrain and/or landscapes, ranging from gentle breezes to strong rushes of wind, often through significant Field Recording use for effect.

name: nocturnal
description: Music that evokes imagery of the night.

name: party
description: Music which evokes imagery associated with parties and partying, be it energetic jams, slow late-nighters, or something in-between.

name: pastoral
description: Music which evokes imagery of the countryside and rural life, such as open fields, rolling hills, farms, and villages.

name: peaceful
description: Music which evokes the imagery of or a sense of peace, tranquillity, or serenity.

name: psychedelic
description: Music that evokes the imagery of or replicates the experience of psychedelic drugs, such as LSD. Characteristics that can be found within psychedelic music include the use of techniques such as reverb, phasing, backward tapes, feedback, and wah wah pedals; instruments such as sitar, tabla, harpsichord, synthesizers, and distorted electric guitars; and the use of complex song structures, modal melodies, and drones as well as themes relating to drugs.

name: ritualistic
description: Music which evokes the ambiance of ritual ceremonies. It induces ecstatic feelings and/or states of trance, and often conjures a primal and/or communal atmosphere.

name: seasonal
description: Seasonal music evokes the imagery of a time of year that is accompanied by a type of weather, including spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

name: autumn
description: Music which evokes the imagery of autumn or fall.

name: spring
description: Music which evokes the imagery of spring, including blooming flowers and foliage, warming temperatures, and celebrations associated with the season.

name: summer
description: Music which evokes the imagery of summer, such as warm days, beaches, summer holidays and celebrations.

name: winter
description: Music which evokes the imagery of winter, such as snow, the cold, fireplaces, and winter holidays and celebrations.

name: space
description: Music which evokes the imagery of outer space, including universe exploration, the dark void, intergalactic wars, alien planets, etc.

name: spiritual
description: Music which evokes spiritual imagery. It can also convey the feelings accompanying a search for a higher plane of being, or a state of bliss found through intense introspective activity.

name: surreal
description: Music which evokes surreal, disorienting, fantastic, or unreal imagery which often mimics the hallucinatory qualities of a dream or the ethereal.

name: suspenseful
description: Music which evokes uncertainty or excitement, or which conveys the anticipation or build-up of a certain outcome.

name: tribal
description: Music which evokes the influence of tribal cultures. Tribal music heavily relies on rhythmic structures and frequently incorporates non-Western traditional instruments. It often has an entrancing or hypnotic atmosphere.

name: twinkling
description: Twinkling music evokes the shine of small, intermittent gleams, such as those of starry skies, crystalline water, or minerals. A twinkling sound is usually achieved with the bright chimes of metal, glass, or plucked or strummed string instruments played in reverberating staccato or arpeggio. It is especially common in Christmas Music, Mechanical Music, Jangle Pop, and Midwest Emo.

name: urban
description: Music which evokes the imagery of a city, especially the lives of urban communities or individual people within a metropolis.

name: warm
description: Music which evokes the sensation of warmth and the associated imagery, such as the desert, tropical areas, or other such landscapes.

name: form
description: A musical form describes an overall structure of a music work. More specifically, a form may define the order and type of various sections within a song, the instruments that are used, and/or other aspects of music composition.

name: ballad
description: The term "ballad" originally refers to songs adapted from narrative poems and composed in short stanzas. With the emergence of popular music, the term also began to be used for slow and usually sentimental love songs.

name: concept album
description: Concept albums are composed of songs focused on a unified common theme or idea, achieved through interlinked narrative structure and/or cohesive musical composition. They are notably unique from standard albums, which are generally not focused on a singular theme, or are - but which do not utilise a sense of connection between the overall songs. Concept albums are not always lyrical, as instrumental albums can still create a connected sense of an individual idea through various compositional techniques.

name: diss
description: A diss is a verbal attack on another person or multiple people, usually another artist. It is typically created to address or escalate a personal feud between the artist and recipient. Disses are most commonly found in hip hop.

name: ensemble
description: An ensemble refers to the group of people who perform music and how they perform it. Ensembles can be categorized by their size or by the type of instruments they use.

name: a cappella
description: A cappella music is performed by solo musicians or a vocal group, who sing without musical accompaniment. Though originally having its roots in religious chants (being Italian for "in the manner of the chapel"), it later became synonymous with the phrase "unaccompanied vocal music". Despite this, some a cappella music does feature minor or light instrumentation, usually in the form of percussive elements.

name: acoustic
description: Acoustic music is played without the use of any electric instruments.

name: choral
description: Choral music is written to be performed by choirs, and is generally performed a cappella, though instrumental accompaniment (or full orchestration) is not uncommon.

name: duet
description: A duet is a type of composition that contains two focal performers playing distinct but complementary musical parts. Duets featuring two vocalists are frequently structured as a conversation between the singers.

name: orchestral
description: Orchestral music is written for and performed by large orchestras, with musicians exceeding the small number found within Chamber Music. The music performed is generally within the realm of Western Classical Music and genres influenced by it.

name: unaccompanied solo
description: The term "unaccompanied solo" refers to music performed by one person with a single instrument or voice, without accompaniment from a backing band, backing track or overdubbing. This often allows for a performer or composer to display their skill with an instrument, or creates a more personal and intimate atmosphere.

name: vocal group
description: Vocal groups consist of a three or more vocalists performing harmonised music in a combined ensemble. Some groups perform a cappella, whilst others utilise a backing band to accompany them.

name: medley
description: A medley is a form of music that combines two or more different musical pieces played in succession.

name: monologue
description: A monologue is a spoken piece presented by a single person, or more often, character. Generally monologues are dramatic, and serve a purpose within a narrative, but are sometimes performed as a form of poetry.

name: parody
description: A musical parody takes elements from established artists, styles, or individual songs and restructures their content lyrically, musically, or by satirizing their intent to create an intentionally humorous or ironic adaptation of the original work(s).

name: pastiche
description: A pastiche is a work deliberately written or performed in the style of another artist, composer, genre, school or period. Pastiche is distinguished from pasticcio (Italian for pie), a type of medley of arias from different operas that emerged in Italy in the late-17th century, as well as from parody, which involves the intent to criticise, satirise or ridicule. This intent is often absent in pastiche, which can be neutral or even affectionate towards its source material.

name: section
description: Sections found within a composition can include the usage of an intro, one or more interlude tracks, occasionally a reprise of an earlier track, and a conclusion or outro.

name: interlude
description: An interlude is a short piece, often instrumental, inserted between songs on an album or between longer movements within a larger composition.

name: intro
description: An intro is the introductory section of a larger compositional piece or album that is usually designed to set the tone and/or introduce the main theme overall.

name: movement
description: Movements are self-contained sections of larger compositions, commonly found in Classical Music but also in some popular genres that often make use of suites, such as Progressive Rock.

name: outro
description: An outro is the opposite of an intro; it is used to conclude a larger compositional piece or to end an album.

name: reprise
description: A reprise is a piece of music which is a reiteration of a previous piece from an earlier stage in a release or composition.

name: silence
description: Silent compositions contain no notes, e.g. consist entirely of pauses (such as John Cage's 4'33"), or are completely soundless tracks that sometimes appear as an interlude between songs on an album.

name: skit
description: Skits are short pieces, typically in the Spoken Word or Sketch Comedy genres and commonly included in Hip Hop projects. While often humorous, they can also serve to develop themes or reinforce a release's concept. King Tee's "Baggin' on Moms," released in November 1988, is considered the first full-length hip hop skit, but the format was popularized by De La Soul the following year on 3 Feet High and Rising. Common skit types include mock radio broadcasts, voicemails, and sex skits.

name: suite
description: A suite is a musical composition which consists of multiple distinct (but linked) movements or pieces which are played in succession.

name: lyrics
description: The lyrics of a song consist of its subject matter or theme and the way they are expressed through the vocalist's tone.

name: code-mixing
description: Code-mixing in music is a lyrical process in which two or more languages are mixed within the same song.

name: dialogue
description: Dialogue in music is a vocal narrative involving two or more people or characters delivering conversational lines or engaging in discussion. Usually theatrical, it can range from spoken word verses to more melodic lines.

name: lyrical dissonance
description: Lyrical dissonance refers to a mismatch between the emotions expressed by the lyrics and the instrumental of a song. Most examples feature upbeat instrumentals with dark lyrics, but it can also refer to tracks with dark instrumentals and positive lyrics.

name: narrative
description: Narrative is a storytelling structure heavily focused on plot; it introduces settings, characters and their motivations, and leads the story toward the outcome through a series of related events.

name: stream of consciousness
description: Stream of consciousness refers to a narrative mode that mimics the rapid flow of thoughts running through the narrator's head. The term was coined in The Principles of Psychology (1890) by psychologist William James to describe the uninterrupted "stream" of thought, but it began to be used to describe a literary technique from the late 1910s onward, notably embraced by modernist-era writers such as James Joyce and Virginia Woolf as well as the Beat Generation. Stream-of-consciousness narratives are typically characterized by nonlinear storytelling, emphasis on sensory perception, occasional repetition of phrases, and an instantaneous "interior monologue" of the narrator's thoughts. In a musical context, this mode can appear in a variety of inflections, themes, and genres of music, but the core tenets of the style stay the same.

name: tone
description: In the context of literature and music lyrics, tone refers to the author's attitude towards a particular subject (theme). Characteristics that contribute to the tone include the choice and arrangements of the words, imagery, details, figurative language, and delivery. It can contribute to the overall mood of the song.

name: apathetic
description: Lyrics with an apathetic tone show very little emotion, causing the writer to seem uninterested, bored or indifferent.

name: boastful
description: Lyrics with a boastful tone will often include heavy amounts of self-satisfaction, big-headedness, and/or egotism. The tone can be either be expressed positively in reference to the singer, their crew, their town, their music, etc. or it can be negative in regard to others when compared to themselves.

name: cautionary
description: Cautionary music serves to warn against certain actions, behaviors, or situations, often by depicting their negative consequences. The cautionary aspect may be conveyed directly through explicit advice, or indirectly through storytelling, confessions, and narration of possible destructive outcomes.

name: cryptic
description: Lyrics with a cryptic tone are mysterious in meaning, or have no clear meaning.

name: hateful
description: Lyrics with a hateful tone reflect the singer's hatred or disdain towards the relevant subject matter.

name: humorous
description: Lyrics with a humorous tone use comedy to reflect a sense of humour towards the relevant subject matter.

name: dark humor
description: Lyrics with dark humor treat serious, bleak, or taboo subjects with irony, cynicism, absurdity, and/or edginess to provoke bitter amusement, as a form of social commentary or as a coping mechanism.

name: insecure
description: Lyrics with an insecure tone show a lack of confidence, assurance and vulnerable feelings of uncertainty or anxiety, usually about oneself.

name: menacing
description: A menacing or threatening tone is one intended to scare the listener and suggest, implicitly or explicitly, that the listener is in danger. This often includes threats of violence by the speaker.

name: misanthropic
description: A misanthropic tone conveys antisocial tendencies, or the dislike of other people.

name: optimistic
description: Lyrics with an optimistic tone reflect the singer's positive feelings towards the relevant subject matter. This can be both an upbeat attitude towards a positive theme, or an optimistic outlook on a negative theme.

name: pessimistic
description: Lyrics with a pessimistic tone reflect the singer's negative feelings towards the relevant subject matter. This can be both an downbeat attitude towards a negative theme, or a pessimistic outlook on a positive theme.

name: poetic
description: Lyrics with a poetic tone are generally charming, are characterized by beauty, and often rhyme or utilize other rules found in styles of poetry. Poetic lyrics may not always be in the form of a poem directly, as any lyrics can be described as sensitively emotional or sublime in this way.

name: provocative
description: Provocative music seeks to create a reaction in its listener, ranging from anger, disgust, and discomfort, to sensationalist intrigue and shock. Typically, provocative music depicts taboo topics like violence or sexuality in a blunt manner, often using vulgar (even offensive) lyricism, but it can also take forms like disturbing, visceral depictions of personal trauma or politically charged attacks on social norms.

name: rebellious
description: Lyrics with a rebellious tone generally reflect the non-conformist, oppositional, and/or disobedient attitude of the singer. Rebellious lyrics often relate to social or political themes.

name: sarcastic
description: Lyrics with a sarcastic tone use irony to mock the relevant subject matter.

name: satirical
description: Satirical music contains lyrics that use irony and exaggeration, often with a sarcastic edge, in order to denounce or ridicule human vices, follies, and flaws.

name: serious
description: Lyrics with a serious tone reflect the singer's solemnity towards the relevant subject matter.

name: vulgar
description: Lyrics with a vulgar tone reflect the singer's lack of good taste or politeness in regards to a (usually taboo) subject matter.

name: mood
description: The mood of music refers to the emotions that are conveyed as a result of listening to it. Mood is distinguished from atmosphere in that the latter is largely associated with imagery, not emotion.

name: style
description: A musical style describes how one or more aspects of music, such as melody, harmony, rhythm, timbre, tempo, dynamics, and form, are used. The word "style" is sometimes used interchangeably with "genre", but it is much more specific and detailed, denoting particular characteristics of music rather than the sound as a whole.

name: angular
description: Angularity in music refers to a particular form of melody where there are large jumps in intervals and sudden shifts in melodic direction, leading to a sense of dissonance and tension due to the resulting jagged textures. Angularity draws its name from its distinct sound, which evokes imagery of sharp angles and zigzagging lines. This form of playing is frequently accompanied by "start-and-stop" rhythms, where the instruments begin and end at irregular moments. Interplay between different instruments is also common, with angular countermelodies often being described as "interlocking." This form of playing is particularly common in Post-Punk, New Wave, and Math Rock, where it is used to create a mechanical, jagged, or uneasy sound.

name: anthemic
description: Anthemic music is made suitably for anthems, with notable characteristics such as containing an easy-to-remember musical theme, utilising call-and-response lyrics, being repetitive, and having a powerful sound.

name: atmospheric
description: Atmospheric music puts special emphasis on the timbre and texture of the music, its "atmosphere". The atmosphere in such music becomes the core of the composition as opposed to the more melodic, rhythmic or technical forms of music.

name: atonal
description: Atonal music can be generally seen as music which lacks focus on a key. Commonly, it is used to describe songs in which notes on a chromatic scale are played independently of one another. The roots of atonal music can be traced to late 19th to early 20th century Classical Music, where composers would seemingly forego the teachings and fundamentals of composition set out during the common practice period (c. 1600-1900). It is also not limited to just forms of Experimental music, but it is found more commonly in leftfield genres due to its mostly criticized practice.

name: avant-garde
description: Avant-garde music deliberately alienates or challenges audiences while pushing the boundaries of what may be acceptable in the cultural realm. Its music is often Experimental, radical, or unorthodox, and may exaggerate methods of recording, composition, or execution to hyperbole. Some quintessential examples are Erik Satie's Vexations (instructs the player to perform a theme 840 times) or John Cage's 4'33" (a three-movement piece consisting of silence). Avant-garde sensibilities can also be found in non-classical work, like that by Sun Ra, The Residents, and Captain Beefheart. Because the avant-garde challenges the status quo in favour of unique or original ideas, it is considered to be at the forefront of experimentation or innovation in its field.

name: bassy
description: Bassy music focuses on frequencies under 200 Hz, usually performed on a bass instrument such as a contrabass, electric bass, or synth bass, or featuring low percussion such as a kick drum. Frequencies under 80 Hz are referred to as sub-bass and are often emphasized in Dance and Hip Hop music. In the vinyl era, bass frequencies were limited by the width of the groove, but the introduction of the compact cassette and the 12-inch vinyl single allowed for greater bass frequency response. Simultaneously, subwoofers capable of reproducing sub-bass were introduced both in discotheques and Jamaican sound systems, leading to bassy music like Dub and Disco, which had a major impact on subsequent producers.

name: buzzy
description: A buzzy style makes use of a continuous low, vibrating sound, similar to that of a bee. Music in this style often adopts certain production choices and techniques, such as the use of synths, as well as distorted percussion. This style can sometimes be perceived as exaggerated or even intense.

name: chaotic
description: Chaotic music is characterised by a sense of disorder, discordance, and confusion.

name: clanging
description: Clanging refers to the sound of forcefully struck metallic instruments such as metallophones, bells, and gongs, as well as other sounds with similar timbres. Traditionally, these sounds feature prominently in Southeast Asian Classical Music, various bell-ringing traditions such as Change Ringing, and in the Western Classical Music tradition through instruments such as tubular bells. Clanging percussion is often used in Industrial music, with various metallic instruments featuring heavily in the music of Einstürzende Neubauten.

name: complex
description: Complex music comprises many elements interconnected in complicated ways, utilizing various changes in any of its aspects, particularly tempo, rhythm, melody, dynamics, and structure.

name: crackly
description: Crackly music uses dry, sharp, unpitched "crackling" sounds in its production. These are often sampled from analog media such as vinyl or tape, but they may also include natural sounds such as fire, acoustic effects such as guitar fret noise or string buzz, voice cracks, and digital effects with similar timbres. These elements may be part of the original recording in lo-fi productions, or they may be added to a higher-fidelity mix as is common in Trip Hop and many styles of Hip Hop.

name: dense
description: Dense music is characterised by an intensive, busy, thick, and often multi-layered sound.

name: dissonant
description: Dissonant music is characterised by a use of harsh and/or inharmonious sound.

name: eclectic
description: Eclectic music combines different techniques, styles, aesthetics, instrumentation, and genres through the duration of a song or entire release.

name: fuzzy
description: Fuzz is characterized by a distorted, heavily saturated sound, changing the signal to a square wave and producing a long-lasting sustain and an occasionally lo-fi sound. It is commonly applied to instruments like guitar and bass through the use of fuzz pedals as seen in Rock offshoots like Psychedelic Rock, Stoner Metal, and Shoegaze. It is also seen in synth-driven Electronic genres like Electropop and Electro House.

name: heavy
description: Heavy music uses techniques such as distorted and downtuned riffs, forceful rhythm section, loud low frequencies, and abrasive and aggressive performance to create a powerful and pounding sound. Metaphorically speaking, it describes music which feels to have a lot of crushing "weight".

name: instrumental
description: Instrumental music usually contains no vocals or lyrics, although some compositions occasionally utilise sampling that contains speech, nonlexical vocables, or short Spoken Word pieces within.

name: lo-fi
description: Lo-fi (short for low fidelity) is a production style in which the recordings are made in a lower quality than was standard for the time in which they were made. This is often done deliberately. However, in other cases, it's simply a consequence of circumstances.

name: lush
description: Lush music uses techniques such as rich textures, layered instrumentation, extended chords, string arrangements, and clean production to create a tender and colourful sound. The Wall of Sound production technique is often utilised to create such a style.

name: maximalist
description: Maximalist music is characterized by a grandiose sound that embraces heterogeneity and excessive use of musical elements, favoring intense dynamics, lush arrangements, thick textures, and extensive instrumentation or studio layering.

name: melodic
description: Melodic music puts strong emphasis on melody compared with other aspects of composition such as rhythm, harmony, or texture. The most prominent feature of melodic music is the dominance of a strong melody line.

name: microtonal
description: Microtonal music can refer either to a tuning system consisting of intervals smaller than the semitone (the smallest interval in standard Western music, often called the "half-step") or, more generally, to any music that does not divide the octave into twelve equal parts.

name: minimalistic
description: Minimalistic music is characterised by a stripped-down sound which keeps only essential sounds, uses predominantly conventional song structures, and narrow instrumentation.

name: monophonic
description: Monophony is considered the simplest musical texture and found in every culture, consisting of a single melody which is not accompanied by harmony or unfixed chords. This is often done with a single voice or instrument. It can also be performed by choirs and ensembles, where the melody is performed in unison, or with performers playing at fixed intervals to account for natural differences in pitch. If monophony is paired with a drone note, it is known as biphony, and if different performers play the same melody with different rhythms or embellishments, it is called heterophony. Monophony can be accompanied by non-melodic percussion.

name: muffled
description: Muffled music typically contains dampened high frequencies, focusing on low and midrange frequencies to create a distant, indistinct, or subdued sound. A muffled sound may result from intentional production techniques such as low-pass filters, reverb, and downsampling, poor recording equipment, physical obstructions between the microphone and sound source, layers of noise that drown out other elements, or the use of lossy audio codecs, such as MP3, in lobit music.

name: noisy
description: Noisy music puts strong emphasis on distorted timbres and textures. This is usually achieved through loud playing, conglomerations of sounds, and/or the extreme application of effects such as echo or fuzz.

name: piercing
description: Piercing music uses very high-pitched, sharp-sounding frequencies. These are often achieved through extreme feedback or notes played well above the typical upper range but may also be caused by other means, such as very bright equalization or a high Q factor. In some cases, the purpose might be to represent the sound of tinnitus, such as in "Ventolin." Due to higher frequencies naturally sounding louder than lower ones at the same volume (an effect known as the Fletcher–Munson curve), some listeners may find these frequencies painful or irritating.

name: polyphonic
description: Polyphonic music utilises multiple simultaneous parts/voices in its composition, through a texture consisting of independent melodic lines, each of similar importance.

name: progressive
description: Progressive music innovates musical conventions through the use of established methods of composition and newer derivative forms and styles. It extensively uses techniques from music theory to create multistructured and/or structurally complex music. In the 20th century, this was initially achieved by using structural unity (formalism), style synthesis, and integration (eclecticism). Newer progressive music has since drawn from various cultural domains, such as Western Classical Music, Celtic Folk Music, South Asian Music, or African Music. Later in the 20th century, the approach led to the creation of Progressive Rock and Progressive Pop, which derived inspiration from techniques in Jazz and Classical Music. Progressive elements may also be found in various music styles and genres that are not explicitly preceded by the term progressive.

name: raw
description: Raw music is characterised by its unrefined, direct delivery and sound, often found in lo-fi recordings as well as genres like Punk / Post-Punk / Hardcore, Slacker Rock, and Hardcore Hip Hop.

name: repetitive
description: Repetitive music focuses on repetition in at least one part of its song structure, such as a repeated loop, riff, melody, hook, or singular note. A number of sub-genres of Electronic Dance Music utilise repetitive patterns, or sequences, through the use of sequencing hardware and software. This is especially notable in House, Techno, and Breakbeat Hardcore (also known as Rave music). In other genres, such as Drone, the entire song itself can be focused on a monotonal and repeated note played throughout the full track. Other genres such as Krautrock and Minimalism are also notable for their frequent use of repetition.

name: rhythmic
description: Rhythmic music puts strong emphasis on rhythm compared with other aspects of composition such as melody, harmony, or texture. The most prominent feature of rhythmic music is the dominance of a strong rhythm section.

name: bouncy
description: A bouncy style features a playful and upbeat back-and-forth rhythm with strong, often syncopated downbeats. It may also incorporate swing rhythms.

name: chugging
description: Chugging is a percussive, rhythmic style of guitar playing that uses palm-muting to create a heavy, low sound. This is usually used for playing straightforward, repetitive riffs.

name: plodding
description: Plodding music has a slow, steady, repetitive beat that is heavy, high in the mix, or otherwise strongly emphasized. This may evoke heavy steps, drudgery, or melancholy.

name: punchy
description: Punchy music is defined by a dynamic rhythmic attack with heavily accented beats, often performed with a staccato or marcato articulation. On the production side, punchiness is defined by transients which cut through a mix, typically consisting of drums or bass instruments. The rhythmic arrangement is typically not very dense so that each attack can provide maximum impact for the listener. Production techniques such as sidechain compression or gated reverb can give a punchy effect.

name: smooth
description: Smooth music is characterized by a highly polished, sleek, and harmonious sound that lacks dissonance and harsh textures. It typically features fluid transitions between notes and a clean production style that creates a rich, spotless quality. Smooth music is commonly found in styles such as Smooth Soul, Contemporary R&B, Adult Contemporary, Soft Rock, and certain strains of Pop and Jazz.

name: soft
description: Soft music is characterised by its light and/or gentle sound, which usually results in a comforting or subdued style.

name: sparse
description: Sparse music is characterised by utilising little sonic activity or variance as well as significant periods of silence and/or near-silence.

name: squelchy
description: Squelchy music resembles the sucking sounds of walking on soft, wet ground. The term is predominantly used to describe Acid House and related genres that feature the Roland TB-303 or synthesizers inspired by it. They use a sawtooth or square wave oscillator and a resonant filter with a fast-attack envelope. This sound is also described as acid. However, other techniques can also lead to a squelchy sound.

name: technical
description: Technical music is characterized by its display of expert skills (instrumental or vocal) by the performers, often through the use of difficult techniques, complex and varied compositions, tempo changes, and uncommon time signatures.

name: theatrical
description: Evokes an extravagant, over-the-top atmosphere, heavily influenced by theater production and typically incorporating musical elements from Musical Theatre and Entertainment.

name: ticking
description: Ticking music uses or recreates the rhythmic clicking sound made by timekeeping devices like clocks, watches and metronomes. This gives the sensation of time passing.

name: warbly
description: Warbly music is characterized by constant fluctuation in frequency or pitch, giving it a warped, unsteady effect. These results are often achieved by effects like wow and flutter.

name: technique
description: The techniques in music describe how it is made, such as the methods and tools used in its composition and production.

name: blast beats
description: Blast beats are a form of frantic, uptempo drum beats that originated in Hardcore [Punk]. Over time, they mainly became associated with genres of extreme metal, such as Black Metal, Grindcore, and Death Metal. A blast beat frequently comprises sixteenth notes divided equally between the snare and bass drum. There are many variations of blast beats, such as bomb blasts, hammer blasts, and gravity blasts, which all differ slightly from the traditional style of blast beats.

name: composition
description: Musical composition refers to the means and methods used to compose a piece of music. Composition itself can occur at any point during a song's 'life', whether through planned writing and playing to a set of musical notation, or composed on-the-fly through improvisation. Using standard (and sometimes non-standard) musical notation, composers create pieces through the standard aspects of music: melody, harmony, form, pitch, dynamics, rhythm, timbre, order, texture, and tempo.

name: aleatory
description: Aleatoric (or chance) music is said to be composed "if its course is determined in general but depends on chance in detail." This is to say, some aspect of the composition (pitch, timbre, tone, notation, etc.) is left to random chance. Aleatoric music is different from improvised music, which is composed "on the fly."

name: call and response
description: Call and response is a compositional technique in which a "call" phrase is performed and then another phrase serves as a "response" to the call. The phrases can be vocal or instrumental as well as composed or improvised; they can be performed by groups or by individual vocalists or instrumentalists. Call and response is prevalent across many cultures and genres. Sometimes derived from African traditions, its influence can be commonly seen in African American Blues and Gospel and also in many Latin American musical traditions, notably Cuban Music, where it is called coro-pregón.

name: free rhythm
description: Free rhythm is a technique in which a regular underlying pulse or pattern of beats (meter) is eschewed in favor of irregular, free-flowing rhythms. The use of free rhythm is rare in Western popular music but is commonly found in various kinds of Experimental music, atmosphere-focused genres, such as Ambient, and a variety of Regional Music styles across the globe.

name: gallop
description: The gallop is a rhythm created by playing an eighth note followed by two sixteenth notes. The rhythm is closely associated with Heavy Metal, with Iron Maiden most famously making use of the gallop.

name: generative music
description: Generative music, a term created by Brian Eno, describes music with a generated composition applied to a musical scale and array of instruments, which cannot be repeated by its creator. It applies to, for example, recordings of musicians performing generated pieces, music created and played digitally with custom algorithmic software, or organic beings/movements/cycles applied to music. Four perspectives are usually placed on generative music; structural (the composition is created from a musical 'grammar' based on a style), behavioral (no musical input), procedural (a procedure/idea is placed on the musical setting before the piece is initiated) and emergent (music created from organic interactions).

name: improvisation
description: Improvised music is composed in the moment, either in the studio or during a live performance. The improvised elements do not necessarily have to cover the entire piece of music - such as the music found in the Free Improvisation genre - but can be singular parts of a larger whole (such as an on-the-fly saxophone solo during a Jazz performance).

name: freestyle
description: Freestyle is a technique in which a rapper improvises lyrics on the spot. It is most commonly performed in Hip Hop, but can also be found in other rapped genres such as Grime. The term came to its current meaning in the early 1990s, with the term simply meaning a rap with no particular topic during the 1980s. Freestyling is often performed solo, in a group called a cypher, or in a battle format.

name: jamming
description: Originating among Jazz musicians playing together outside of gigs, jamming refers to a spontaneous form of improvisation in which musicians improvise in a more casual and social manner than is common in other improvisational forms. There is typically less enforced structure or limits on the improv, with jams being capable of being either incredibly prolonged or curt, meaning songs are generally created through improvisation, as opposed to the improv just being a section of a larger, more structured and arranged piece. The key component of jamming is its social aspect, with musicians playing off one another and collaborating on a jam live, as opposed to just emphasizing the position of a single, soloing musician. As can be expected from the name, Jam Band music makes extensive use of jamming techniques.

name: polyrhythm
description: Polyrhythmic music simultaneously uses two or more contrasting rhythmic pulses within a piece. Polyrhythms were a defining feature of sub-Saharan and West African Music and were important in the development of genres like Gamelan, Jazz, Samba, and Minimalism.

name: through-composed
description: Through-composed form is a type of musical structure that is continuous, cyclical, and nonrepetitive. Unlike most musical forms, which rely on repetition (such as the verse-chorus (ABAB) or sonata (ABA)), pieces that are through-composed will avoid revisiting sections once they've finished (ABCD...), although some composers might still make use of motifs or recurring themes to give the pieces a greater sense of cohesion. While the term is most commonly applied to vocal songs, it can also be used to describe instrumental compositions.

name: uncommon time signatures
description: In music, meter refers to the regular pattern of strong and weak beats within a piece (often expressed notationally through a time signature). Most Western music can be sorted into the categories of duple meter, triple meter, and quadruple meter, which divide each measure into 2, 3, or 4 equal subdivisions, respectively. These include "simple" meters such as 2/2, 3/4, and 4/4, as well as "compound" meters with a triplet subdivision per beat, such as 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8. Meters that do not fit into the above categories may be called "complex," "irregular," "uncommon," or "odd," though definitions of these terms sometimes vary. A complex meter often takes the form of a repeating pattern combining groups of 2 and 3; for example, 5/4 is often felt as a group of 3 beats followed by a group of 2 beats. Much more intricate patterns are also possible. Complex meters are relatively uncommon in Western popular music but are used in a variety of other styles. Modern Classical composers such as Igor Stravinsky extensively used complex meters with frequent time signature changes in works like Le sacre du printemps [The Rite of Spring]. Complex meters are also commonplace in various technically oriented Rock and Metal subgenres, ranging from Progressive Rock to Technical Death Metal, as well as certain styles of Regional Music, such as Balkan Folk Music.

name: leitmotif
description: Leitmotifs are short, recurring musical phrases meant to be associated with a particular character, place, concept, or idea within a narrative work. They are often modified or expanded upon throughout a work while still remaining easily recognizable as the same musical idea. Leitmotifs are most commonly found within Classical Music, especially Operas, as well as in Soundtracks.

name: production
description: Music production encompasses a variety of techniques used to create a specific or desired sound. This can include standard elements such as fidelity and bitrate, but can extend to specific production techniques such as Phil Spector's Wall of Sound or Frank Zappa's Xenochrony.

name: lobit
description: Lobit music is encoded at a low bitrate – usually 64kbps or lower – using a lossy audio codec (e.g. MP3) in order to achieve data compression and make the music sound blocky and glitchy.

name: sampling
description: Sampling is a production technique in which an artist or band lifts a portion of a pre-existing sound recording and reuses it in a new piece. Samples can range from anything from milliseconds of audio (such as is found in Micromontage music), to complete songs being reused in new ways (such as in Plunderphonics). While most samples generally consist of a percussive pattern or vocal clip, samplers have used almost every conceivable piece of audio in order to create new music. Sampling dates as far back as the 1950s, where Musique concrète and Tape Music artists experimented with manipulation of tape loops. It further developed when Sound Collage began creating artistic compositions made (usually) entirely from previous sound material. Through the 1960s and 1970s, Experimental Rock and Punk / Post-Punk / Hardcore bands began to use sampling in more commonplace music. Industrial music brought the use of home-made sampling devices, and soon after commercial samplers became more publicly available. The use of sampling in more popular music was further expanded on with the rise of Hip Hop in the late 1970s and 1980s. Artists began more commonly lifting samples of previous works into new compositions, and Electronic music saw more prominent uses of the technique. Today, sampling can be heard in almost every genre of music, as sampling equipment and digital software makes it possible for any artist to use it in their music.

name: vocal chops
description: Vocal chops are cleanly cut and usually very short vocal samples that are generally rearranged or repeated to create a melody or rhythm distinct in sound from the original sample.

name: Wall of Sound
description: The Wall of Sound (or Spector Sound) is a production formula developed by producer-songwriter Phil Spector in the 1960s. It involves many acoustic/electric guitars, keyboards, and percussive instruments playing in unison. The resultant sound would then be mixed closely together and accentuated with reverb. The Wall of Sound was built from carefully-blended instrumental colors, as opposed to simply raising the levels of multiple instruments to the point of distortion. Use of layered channels of monaural sound, blended together in a carefully arranged way are core to the overall sound, and is essential to avoid a busy or overly dense sound. Other producers and artists, most notably Brian Wilson, have adopted the technique.

name: reversing
description: Reversing is an effect made by playing an audio recording backward. This technique was first employed by Musique concrète composers in the 1950s with the manipulation of magnetic tape and then popularized by psychedelic music in the '60s. Modern music makes use of software and digital audio to achieve the effect.

name: rubato
description: Tempo rubato (Italian for stolen time; often shortened to rubato) is a phrasing technique in which the tempo of a piece is sped up and slowed down at the performer's or conductor’s discretion, while still retaining the same pace overall. This ebbing and flowing of time creates a sound that is both more natural and more expressive than a straight tempo performance, which may be seen as lacking nuance or emotion in comparison. Rubato is often associated with Romanticism, especially the works of Frédéric Chopin, but is also used in certain strains of Jazz, as well as the traditional music of various regions (with Polish Folk Music, for instance, having influenced Chopin's use of rubato).

name: tone clusters
description: Tone clusters, also known as cluster chords, are dissonant note combinations that are formed by playing multiple adjacent notes at the same time. Traditionally, tone clusters are a standard element in Gagaku. However, because of their dissonance, these chords were uncommon in Western music until the early 20th century, when they began to be used by early Modern Classical composers, most notably Henry Cowell. Tone clusters saw significant adoption by jazz pianists, especially those associated with Avant-Garde Jazz, such as Cecil Taylor. Less dissonant uses of tone clusters in jazz piano were developed by artists such as Bill Evans. Composers like György Ligeti and Eric Whitacre incorporated tone clusters into orchestral and choral arrangements, respectively.

name: theme
description: A theme is a prominent or recurring topic, subject, idea, or message of the music. Themes range from concepts that the work is about to statements that it makes about them. Themes are commonly expressed through the lyrics, but certain sounds, styles, works, and imagery can be used to reference associated places, cultures, events, periods, etc. In interpretation and art studies, the theme of the work is often understood more narrowly as the underlying message or insight communicated through the subject matter. It can be divided into two parts: thematic concept and thematic statement. Thematic concept refers to ideas and aspects of the human condition that are explored in the work, while thematic statement implicitly or explicitly conveys the artist's perspective on them. In broader, colloquial usage, the subject of the work in general — that is, the things that it is "about" — is also referred to as the theme.

name: about music
description: Music featuring lyrical themes about music itself. Themes can include, but are not limited to, listening to music, showing appreciation for music, tributes to other musicians, the act of making and performing music, or being a musician in general.

name: abstract
description: Abstract themes are broad overall, but generally refer to cryptic lyricism of a variety of subjects. They can range from the everyday to the extreme, or be a nonsensical combination of the two. Allegory and metaphorical expressionism are also common in abstract lyrics.

name: adolescence
description: Music about adolescence captures the experiences felt by people between the start of puberty and the beginning of adulthood, commonly exploring topics such as angst, rebellion and coming of age.

name: afterlife
description: The afterlife refers to the continuation of a conscious existence after death. It may take place in a spiritual realm, through reincarnation, or as a ghostly presence in this world.

name: ghosts
full_path: theme > afterlife > ghosts | theme > paranormal > ghosts
description: Music which describes the presence of ghostly entities, ranging from antagonistic ghosts haunting the living to friendly spirits of loved ones.

name: ageing
description: Ageing covers a variety of topics connected to growing older. Examples include songs about coming of age and transitioning from childhood to adulthood, reflecting on one's current age in comparison to one's youth, and confronting one's own mortality. More broadly, this also includes any song that covers the effects of time on a person and their relationships.

name: alienation
description: Themes of alienation revolve around being alienated in one's environment, society, or even self.

name: aliens
description: Thematic content about aliens deals with representation of imaginary or supposed beings originating from worlds beyond Earth. These may be accounts of contact with extraterrestrial life or stories about extraterrestrial civilizations, and these life forms may be depicted as advanced, primitive, benevolent, hostile, or simply mysterious. The theme may relate to science fiction, the paranormal, mystical imagery, or existential reflections.

name: alter ego
description: Alter egos are constructed performing identities or characters assumed by an artist. Such personas are often used by artists for theatrical purposes or to explore a performing identity or musical style differing from that which they are most known for.

name: apology
description: Music that revolves around recognizing the wrong in one's actions and making amends. Such music may express remorse, convey sympathy for the victim, describe atonement for one's actions, and seek forgiveness and reconciliation.

name: aviation
description: Music with an aviation theme focuses on building and operating aircraft, air travel, and related aspects of mechanical flight, like airports, pilots, and various experiences of flying.

name: beauty
description: Beauty is an aesthetic judgment that deems an object, person, or experience pleasant or attractive. Music may feature various themes about beauty. A popular lyrical theme is the beauty of a person, such as a loved one or potential partner in romantic songs or of oneself as an expression of self-love. Other common subjects include the beauty of the natural world and religious or spiritual experience.

name: betrayal
description: Themes of betrayal explore the breaking of trust or loyalty between two or more parties, often involving deception, disloyalty, or the violation of expectations within personal or social relationships.

name: infidelity
full_path: theme > betrayal > infidelity | theme > love > infidelity
description: Music about unfaithfulness to a romantic or sexual partner. Topics can include being cheated on, being a cheater, or simply doubt that one's partner is being faithful.

name: birthday
description: Birthdays are most commonly recognized for people, as well as for animals and (figuratively) institutions. Celebrations popular across many cultures can include parties, gifts, cards, or a ceremony denoting a specific rite of passage. Some birthdays also have religious connotations, such as Christmas or Buddha Day.

name: boredom
description: Boredom is an unpleasant emotion characterised by a lack of interest in one's own surroundings, often caused by a lack of stimulation.

name: callback
description: Artists may reference their own work as a form of introspection, to tie together different projects, or simply as an Easter egg for listeners.

name: childhood
description: Music themed around children typically explores the experience of childhood, ranging from activities like school or play to personal childhood experiences, as well as broader observations about childhood overall. It may be presented from the perspective of a child, an adult caring for a child, or adult reminiscence and reflection on their own childhood experiences.

name: circus
description: Music with a circus theme focuses on cheerful, over-the-top, and sometimes chaotic fairs that feature merry-go-rounds, clowns, circus animals, acrobats, ringmasters, and marching bands. Some music offers a more sinister interpretation of the circus theme by including figures like evil clowns.

name: community
description: Themes of community focus on groups of people sharing common characteristics or interests, as well as the bonds, struggles, and shared experiences that tie people together. It can include feelings of celebration and togetherness, solidarity in hardship, or the loss of connection and belonging.

name: conscious
description: Socially conscious lyrics describe how political, cultural, economical, religious, and other social factors influence the lives of people within a society. Such lyrics are often critical of what causes day-to-day struggles of ordinary people. They generally attempt to convey a positive message, and raise social and personal awareness.

name: antiracism
description: Antiracism includes ideas and actions opposing racial prejudice, racial oppression, and systemic racism. Music has long been a significant medium for antiracist messaging, alongside other egalitarian movements like feminism, anticolonialism, and antiwar movements. Antiracist music may include explicit calls for antiracist action, taking the form of protest music, or may otherwise decry the conditions faced by those subject to racial prejudice and oppression.

name: conspiracy
description: Conspiracy involves secretive actions by groups or organizations aiming to achieve harmful or malevolent objectives. This may include works that believe in, critique, or fictionalize conspiracies, whether based on proven or unproven theories.

name: courage
description: Music with a theme of courage is about the willingness to confront pain, danger, or uncertainty. One type of courage, known as valor, is showing strength when faced with physical pain or the threat of death in the midst of a battle. Another is acting with proper morals and ethics, even when making unpopular decisions that are subject to public opposition, risking shame, scandal, discouragement, or some form of personal loss. Courage, translated as fortitude and mixed with perseverance and patience, is one of the classical virtues of philosophy.

name: crime
description: Themes of crime cover a variety of subjects within criminal law. These can include violence and murder, stealing, rioting, drugs, etc.

name: death
description: Themes of death relate to situations surrounding death. These can include the loss of a friend, family member, or loved one, fears of one's own death, or suicide.

name: homicide
full_path: theme > death > homicide | theme > violence > homicide
description: Music that includes topical or lyrical reference to taking another's life, including the desire or intent to do so.

name: suicide
description: Music that includes topical or lyrical references to the act of killing oneself, including the desire or intent to do so. Self-harm is often explored in a similar vein. Lyrics that discuss such topics tend to have a self-hating, lonely, mournful, or misanthropic tone.

name: decay
description: Mostly meant to describe a physical rot or weathering, decay is often used as a theme in music for messages of aging and increased fragility over time. Sometimes, the decay is that of living things; other times, it is of objects. Occasionally, this theme is expressed lyrically, though it has been used often in Experimental and Classical Music as a theme of composition. When used as a compositional theme, it is often through aleatory means rather than direct, intentional decay or harm, though both have been used.

name: disappointment
description: The theme of disappointment focuses on the negative emotion derived from failed hopes or expectations. It differs from regret because it focuses on the outcome, rather than one's own choices, in a given situation. Some suggest disappointment causes both psychological stress and strain on the immune system. It is a common feeling among those who take risks and attempt to avoid underwhelming results.

name: disaster
description: Disasters are sudden, accidental events that adversely affect lives, livelihoods, or places, often resulting in permanent changes to societies, flora and fauna, environments, and more. These incidents often require external assistance necessary to manage the impacts and hardships they produce.

name: drought
description: Drought is a prolonged lack of rain due to abnormal or periodic conditions. It can be responsible for various forms of human suffering and environmental harm, including agricultural and ecological disruption, thirst, famine, forced migrations, and wildfires.

name: domestic
description: Domestic themes relate to a home environment, daily household activities, or domestic intimacy or describes such an environment.

name: drugs
description: Themes of drugs generally relate to the acquisition and/or consumption of legal and illegal drugs. These can range from alcohol, to the more common usage of marijuana, all the way up to harder illegal drugs such as heroin. Many songs (especially those relating to the usage of LSD or marijuana) often carry a strong psychedelic sound.

name: alcohol
description: Themes about alcohol range from merry drinking songs, to party anthems about getting drunk, but can also be sombre and reflect on issues with alcoholism.

name: antidrug
description: Antidrug sentiment can include the idealistic promotion of abstinence and sobriety and the desire to legally ban or outlaw such materials. Antidrug lyrics also encompass expressions of regret and disavowal made by those who are struggling or have struggled with drug use or addiction as well as those who have overcome drug addiction by ceasing drug use.

name: cannabis
description: Cannabis themes focus on the psychoactive drug derived from the cannabis plant and its related stoner culture. This may include discussion of preparation, purchase, sale, or consumption of the drug, including the "high" it causes.

name: cocaine
description: Cocaine is a theme in music about the psychostimulant drug derived from the leaves of South American coca plants. It may include discussion of the various ways of preparing and consuming the drug, the illegal drug trade (including narco life topics), and sociopolitical commentary on its impact on communities and governments.

name: hallucinogens
description: Hallucinogens are psychoactive drugs that produce altered states of consciousness, often causing major changes in thought, mood, and perception. They can usually be categorised as psychedelics, dissociatives, or deliriants, though some do not fall into these three classes.

name: nicotine
description: As one of the world's most widespread drugs and a mainstay in popular culture, nicotine frequently finds its way into music. Songs may reference the communal aspects of nicotine consumption, its calming nature, its addictive qualities, or its deleterious effects on the human body.

name: dystopian
description: Dystopian music features a bleak society, often an authoritarian surveillance state set in an imagined future reality.

name: cyberpunk
full_path: theme > dystopian > cyberpunk | theme > science fiction > cyberpunk
description: Cyberpunk is a literary subgenre of science fiction that depicts technologically advanced dystopian societies in which the deep integration of technology into everyday life coexists with social and moral decay under the domination of megacorporations. Recurring themes include information technology, artificial intelligence, hacking, human–machine interfaces, cybernetics and virtual reality.

name: educational
description: Educational themes are generally simple, and are usually designed in such a way as to teach people through the medium of song.

name: entertainment industry
description: Music about the entertainment industry reflects on the culture and entertainment business, including artists, record labels, producers, consumers, and the media. Lyrics may criticize exploitation, the standardization of content, the pressures for commercial success, and conformity to mainstream standards, as well as celebrate positive aspects of it or highlight the activities behind the scenes. They may also address socially cultivated illusions or the emotional consequences of the business.

name: envy
description: A lyrical theme about desiring the perceived better life of someone else, often accompanied by a feeling of inferiority or a desire for revenge.

name: escapism
description: Escapism themes focus on intentional detachment from unpleasant emotions or harsh aspects of daily life, usually by engaging in fantasy or enjoying entertainment.

name: everyday life
description: Themes of everyday life consist of day-to-day activities and mundane experiences, often without significant drama or conflict.

name: failure
description: Failure is about being unable to reach an intended goal or meet expectations. This often includes reflection on the moments when effort and ambition confront reality. Typical emotions accompanying failure are disappointment, frustration, and resignation.

name: fairy tale
description: Fairy tales are short, fantastical stories that typically feature elements of folklore and are aimed at children.

name: fame
description: Music about being famous. Topics include the pursuit of fame, the cost of fame and scrutiny by public and the media.

name: family
description: Music about family and familial relationships. This can include immediate family like a spouse, parents, or siblings, as well as more distant relationships like grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins, and so on.

name: fantasy
description: Themes of fantasy are generally fictional narratives set in a fantastical, imaginary universe. They can include elements of magic, mythical beings, sword and sorcery, etc.

name: farewell
description: Music with a farewell theme centers on leaving, saying goodbye, or final moments. It may range from well-wishing and celebratory to negative and uncertain.

name: fashion
description: Themes of fashion reference forms of dress and visual aesthetics that characterize certain social groups or periods of time.

name: cosmetics
description: Cosmetics are substances that are utilized to enhance appearance, increase attractiveness, cover or change certain features, or supplement personal care. They are derived from chemical compounds of either a natural or synthetic source.

name: jewelry
description: Decorative worn items, such as rings, bracelets, and necklaces, typically made of materials like gold, silver, or diamond, often referenced in music as symbols of excess or display of wealth.

name: fear
description: Music with a theme of fear depicts dread, apprehension, and vulnerability caused by a present or anticipated threat. It centers the experience of being afraid, even when the music is not frightening itself.

name: flirting
description: Flirting implies verbal and/or nonverbal communication for humans to engage with each other, whether just for fun or for establishing a more intimate connection. This behavior can escalate, once interest in a long-term romantic or sexual relationship is established. Forms of flirtation can include sensibly playful attitudes, along uses of irony and double entendres. Coquetry can vary with a particular culture's gendered roles or other social norms, such as appropriate levels of touching, physical proximity to one another, and the adequate length of maintaining eye contact.

name: folklore
description: Lyrics influenced by or based on folklore take their story, message, and/or theme from traditional folk literature, poetry, music, art, and/or customs.

name: food
description: Music about food and drink uses lyrics that describe meal preparation (e.g., cooking, baking), feature eating and drinking, or evoke imagery of nutritious substances.

name: freedom
description: The theme of freedom focuses on a person or a group of people being able to act without any outside interference or control. This can refer to physical freedom from imprisonment or confinement, political freedom from oppression, or personal freedom, having autonomy and being generally unconstrained by other people.

name: friendship
description: Music about friendship and friends. Topics include, but are not limited to, platonic love, the importance and celebration of friendship, relationships between friends, and stories about friends or friendship.

name: feminism
full_path: theme > gender > feminism | theme > ideology > feminism
description: Feminism is a range of ideologies focused on systematic gender oppression and the study of gender, formulated by feminist theory. The main points of feminist discussion are patriarchy, intersectionality, sexual harassment, domestic violence, and reproductive rights. Feminism originated with suffragettes in the late 1800s (although anarchist feminism began in the same time period) among upper-class white women. They pushed for rights in voting, politics, work, education, and more, as they had far fewer rights than men. Since then, the movement has gone through numerous waves, expanding its scope to Black and LGBT+ women, as well as other marginalized women, such as women with disabilities. LGBT+ people associated with the feminist movement proved themselves to be quintessential in the fight for LGBT+ rights and the study of sexuality, leading to what is commonly called queer theory.

name: gender dysphoria
full_path: theme > gender > gender dysphoria | theme > health > mental health > gender dysphoria

name: manhood
description: Themes of manhood discuss men's experiences of their gender identity and/or sex. This may involve men's introspection about their gender identity, topics like machismo, the exploration of society's attitudes toward men, and the examination of related political movements.

name: nonbinary
full_path: theme > gender > nonbinary | theme > LGBTQ > nonbinary
description: Nonbinary themes discuss nonbinary people's experiences related to their gender identity. Nonbinary is often used as an umbrella term used to describe people who do not fully identify with one "binary" gender (i.e., male or female). Nonbinary people may identify more with the culture or aesthetics of one gender—or lack any sort of gender experience at all. This theme may include discussion of nonbinary people's transition experiences, introspection about their gender identity, and exploration of society's attitudes toward nonbinary people.

name: transgender
full_path: theme > gender > transgender | theme > LGBTQ > transgender
description: Transgender themes discuss transgender people's experiences related to their gender identity. This includes people whose gender differs from their assigned sex at birth and who consider themselves transgender. This theme may involve discussion of trans people's transition experiences or introspection about their gender identity as well as exploration of society's attitudes toward transgender people and related political movements.

name: womanhood
description: Themes of womanhood discuss women's experiences related to their gender identity and/or sex. This may involve women's introspection about their gender identity as well as exploration of society's attitudes toward women and related political movements.

name: greed
description: Greed can be motivated by a need for personal or family survival, as well as a way to obstruct and deny specific opportunities for one's competitors, especially if said competition is presented as a threat. There can also be dissatisfaction with what one has, even if it meets certain needs, because there is an inability to control one's wants and desires to acquire or possess more.

name: grief
description: Grief involves coping with loss, especially the passing of a loved one or someone important. While commonly associated with death, grief can also arise from other life events, including the loss of employment, a relationship, a marriage, community, health, or an identity.

name: guns
description: Guns are weapons that use pressure or explosive force to propel a projectile, widely used in military, hunting, personal defense, and criminal activities.

name: health
description: Music about the various states of wellness of living things. The most common categories of health are physical and mental health, but there are other recognized aspects of health (e.g., spiritual, social, etc.). Music about health can also be about maintaining good health or awareness of risk factors that impact health, such as genetics or social environments. This theme can focus on any individual living organisms, as well as broader concepts related to the natural world, but most often, this theme is used to discuss human health.

name: disease
description: Music that describes or evokes imagery of catching, suffering from, and dying from diseases and illnesses. Lyrics or samples are oftentimes used to reinforce these themes.

name: fitness
description: Fitness themes focus on physical well-being, exercise, and an active, healthy lifestyle. They highlight discipline and self-improvement through physical activity, sometimes including topics like a well-balanced diet and other healthy habits.

name: injury
description: Injury is physiological damage to the tissue of a living being—for example, breaking one's leg.

name: mental health
description: Mental health themes address one's mental health state regarding their experience of reality and explore topics about psychological well-being, including self-care, recovery and experiences with depression, anxiety, mental disorders, and healing processes, often discussing internal struggles or social stigma.

name: addiction
description: Themes of addiction explore physical and/or mental dependency on a substance or activity. This most commonly relates to alcohol, drugs, or sex but can cover a wide range of topics.

name: trauma
description: Trauma is a severe and lasting emotional shock and pain caused by an extremely upsetting experience. It may convey feelings of vulnerability, fragmentation, or catharsis.

name: sobriety
description: Music about sobriety focuses on a musician's refusal to partake in recreational drug use. Songs that deal with this theme can range from promotion and celebration of the lifestyle to deep introspection on recovery and the struggles of becoming clean. Music-based subcultures such as the Straight Edge movement from the DC hardcore scene emerged in the early '80s advocating a drug-free lifestyle, which inspired various songs rejecting the cultural acceptance of alcohol and other drug use. Many adherents of the movement also went on to adopt much broader definitions of the term that involved abstaining from substances such as caffeine and prescription drugs.

name: hedonism
description: Hedonism is a theme that largely focuses on the pursuit of pleasure and self-gratification, especially sensual self-indulgence. It may include the use of alcohol and recreational drugs, dancing, partying, or sex.

name: history
description: Historical themes revolve around notable past events, people, places, and things.

name: antiquity
description: Antiquity is the period of history between prehistory and the Middle Ages, characterised by ancient civilisations such as Egypt, Greece, Rome, Mesopotamia, and Mesoamerica.

name: prehistory
description: Prehistory is the vast era of early human civilization prior to recorded history, beginning with the first use of stone tools and ending with the invention of the first writing systems. It includes periods like the Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Ice Age.

name: holiday
description: Holiday themes can either refer to a desire to take (or an enjoyment taken from having) a holiday, or to actual holidays themselves such as Christmas and Halloween.

name: Carnaval
description: Carnaval (or Carnival) is a festival season that usually occurs before the Christian Lent period. It is often celebrated with public parades and parties in countries with a Christian majority, where it developed into different regional forms among cities in North America (including the Caribbean), Latin America (including Brazil), and Europe, with leading participants wearing extravagant costumes and masks. Themes of local traditions, partying, and feasting are often prevalent in music celebrating the holiday. In the United States, it is most prevalent in Mardi Gras, the last Tuesday before Lent. It is also referred to as Shrovetide in regions with an Anglican or Protestant majority.
