Some regions observe Carnival festivities months before or after the Lent period, as is the case with Caribbean territories like Antigua and Trinidad.

name: Christmas
description: Christmas themes revolve around the Christian holiday and the winter season. They are often found in Carols.

name: Halloween
description: Halloween lyrics revolve around several traditions of the yearly holiday, such as trick-or-treating, being scary, carving pumpkins, dressing up, etc. Though generally meant to be spooky, these songs are often playful and silly.

name: homesickness
description: Music with a theme of homesickness is about the emotional distress caused by separation from home and familiar environments.

name: horror
description: Horror is a theme in which fictional stories focus on creating fear, shock, and/or repulsion. To this end, these stories may rely on several means, including tales of the supernatural, psychological decline, or extreme violence. They regularly involve monsters such as vampires, ghosts, witches, or zombies.

name: cosmic horror
description: Cosmic horror, also known as eldritch horror or Lovecraftian horror, emphasizes feelings of horror at the unnatural (or eldritch) and incomprehensible. Common themes include cosmic dread, forbidden and ancient knowledge, madness and the insignificance or helplessness of humanity. It originated as a literary genre with the works of H.P. Lovecraft, who in his works developed a mythos (commonly known as the Cthulhu mythos) centered around ancient, monstrous and otherworldly entities. Lovecraft's works inspired a distinct genre in subsequent Horror, Fantasy and weird fiction, which crossed into comics, film and television (see Cosmic Horror); the genre has since had an influence on music as well, particularly in Metal and Dark Ambient.

name: ideology
description: Ideological themes relate to the beliefs and ideas of a group or individual.

name: pacifism
description: Pacifism is the belief that violence and/or war are never justifiable and that disputes should always be peacefully resolved. This usually appears in songs as an expressly anti-war sentiment (e.g., "War") or a general statement against violence (e.g., "Where Is the Love?").

name: pagan
description: Pagan themes espouse pre-Christian, polytheistic folk religions, or modern religious movements inspired by these traditions. Pagan music often also features themes of nature, mythology, and the occult.

name: political
description: Political themes relate to issues within politics, and can include subjects such as nationalism, feelings towards a political leader or party, or anarchism.

name: anarchism
description: Anarchism is a political philosophy which advocates self-governed societies with voluntary institutions. A surge of popular interest in anarchism occurred during the 1970s in the United Kingdom following the birth of Punk Rock.

name: anticolonialism
description: Anticolonialism is resistance to colonialism — domination of one group of people and their territory by another. Music has long been an avenue of anticolonial resistance, either as a platform for critiquing and protesting colonial injustices or as a means of preserving or establishing shared cultural traditions in the face of cultural hegemony and erasure. Examples include the tradition of spirituals that emerged among enslaved African people in the Americas and the establishment of folk orchestras in postcolonial states specializing in Indigenous styles of music while rejecting of the dominance of Western classical music.

name: conservatism
description: Conservatism is a broadly defined political ideology that is historically associated with right-wing politics. Conservatism emphasizes traditionalism, seeking to promote and maintain traditional customs, values, and institutions.

name: environmentalism
full_path: theme > ideology > political > environmentalism | theme > nature > environmentalism
description: Environmentalism is a political and social movement that advocates for protecting and preserving the natural environment, often addressing issues such as industrialization, climate change, and deforestation.

name: nationalism
description: Themes of nationalism focus on strong identification with and pride in one's country or people, often to the exclusion of others. It often emphasizes a collective identity, unique culture, and shared heritage while supporting self-determination and independent political statehood.

name: propaganda
description: Propaganda as a theme is communicated in an attempt to persuade the listener towards a particular cause or point of view. Standard propaganda is typically spread by governments and other political groups.

name: protest
description: Protest songs are generally made within political activist groups in an attempt to promote social change or express concern about political issues. Common and notable examples of protests have included those for LGBTQ rights, women's rights, civil rights, environmentalism, veganism, etc.

name: revolution
description: Due to their fundamental nature throughout human history, usual large scale and intensity, and importance to many political ideologies, revolution has been the subject of a large amount of music. Such music may praise or condemn the aims of revolutionaries or the new political system arising from a revolution, or discuss aspirations of a revolution which has not taken place. The former often crosses with themes of war and propaganda, whilst the latter is usually created alongside protest songs.

name: socialism
description: Socialism is a left-wing political ideology that advocates for public ownership of the means of production, generally with the goal of a classless and egalitarian society.

name: religious
description: Religious themes are generally drawn from or related to religious texts or systems of belief, or they are a form of praise towards one's chosen deity. Early religious music was often ritualistic, though modern praise music is generally more upbeat and lively.

name: Bahá'í
description: Bahá'í themes incorporates elements from the teachings and texts of the Bahá'í faith. The lyrical content can be explored in music incorporating the Bahá'í themes (e.g., the unity of God, religious unity) and texts (e.g., Kitáb-i-Aqdas, Kitáb-i-Íqán). Music by artists such as Seals & Crofts and Do'a was influenced by the Bahá'í faith, as featured in their lyrics.

name: Buddhist
description: Buddhist themes incorporate elements from the teachings and texts of the Buddhist faith. While frequently connected to Buddhist Music, music of any genre can incorporate Buddhist themes. Buddhist chanting is a common devotional practice and can be performed solo or in a group. Other ways in which Buddhism can appear in music include the incorporation of Buddhist philosophy (desire and suffering, nirvana, the Eightfold Path) or the adaptation of traditional Buddhist tales.

name: Christian
description: Christian themes incorporate elements from the teachings and texts of the Christian faith.

name: Hindu
description: Hindu themes incorporate elements from the teachings and texts of the Hindu faith. This can manifest in lyrical content derived from traditional Hindu religious practices (e.g., the chanting of Hindu mantras), the adaptation of Hindu tales and stories, or the expression of Hindu philosophy (e.g., dharma, reincarnation, Brahman).

name: Islamic
description: Islamic themes incorporate elements from the teachings and texts of the Islamic faith.

name: Jain
description: Jain themes incorporates elements from the teachings and texts of the Jain faith. The content can be explored in music incorporating the Jain themes (e.g., asceticism, nonabsolutism, nonviolence) and texts (e.g., Jain Agamas, Satkhandagama, Tattvartha Sutra).

name: Judaic
description: Judaic themes incorporates elements from the teachings and texts of the Judaic faith. Music has played an important role in Judaism since the biblical period. The lyrical content derives from the liturgical practices of the Judaic faith (e.g., chanting, reciting). Secular Judaic genres, such as Klezmer and Muzika mizrahit, were influenced by Judaism as some of the music featured lyrics and sounds that were influenced by chanting, reciting, and texts of the Judaic faith (e.g., Tanakh, Talmud).

name: Rastafari
description: Rastafari themes incorporates elements from the teachings and texts of the Rastafari faith. The lyrical content can be explored in music incorporating the Rastafari themes (e.g., the faith in Jah, Haile Selassie I as the messiah, the return to Africa as Zion) and texts (e.g., Holy Bible, Holy Piby). While linked to Nyahbinghi, Rastafarianism influenced secular Jamaican genres such as Reggae as they featured the lyrics that were influenced by the teachings and texts of the Rastafari faith.

name: Sikh
description: Sikh themes incorporate elements from the teachings and texts of the Sikh faith. Music has been an important part of Sikhism since its beginnings. A notable example of this is that the founder of the religion, Guru Nanak, and his companion, Bhai Mardana, are often depicted as musicians, the former as a lyricist and singer and the latter as a rabab player. Many of the gurus that followed added to the religious musical tradition of the Sikhs, forming the faith's main musical tradition, Shabad kirtan. Other related traditional Sikh religious music forms also developed, including akhand kirtani and istri satsang. Some artists also added Sikh lyrics and influences to modern popular music in styles such as Bhangra and Hip Hop. An example of this was the Shaheedi Immortality series by the label Immortal Productions. Some Western musicians also converted and began producing Sikh music, notably Snatam Kaur, who creates Westernised New Age Kirtan.

name: satanism
description: Music about satanism may include worship or praise of Satan either theistically or nontheistically. It is sometimes associated with specific teachings, such as the philosophical teachings of the nontheistic Church of Satan. Many musicians performatively engage with such themes for their transgressive nature.

name: vegetarianism
description: Vegetarianism is a dietary practice of abstaining from eating meat, often adopted for ethical, environmental, religious or health reasons.

name: indigeneity
description: Music about indigeneity contains content or provides historical context about indigenous communities. Indigenous people are those descended from the original inhabitants of their territories, especially territories that have been colonized. Their music is usually, though not necessarily, traditional folk music. Such music often appears in the same context and style as broader popular music, but it can be distinct from the music of other groups in thematic content, contain subtle or clear influence from traditional music, and circulate in different communities. Music about indigeneity can be distinct from urban, suburban, or pastoral music, often owing to historical and geographical differences. It can also coincide with themes of antiracism, community, family, and history.

name: individuality
description: Themes of individuality center on the recognition of one's identity and the things that distinguish oneself from others. It can include celebration of what makes people unique, resistance to conformity, or feelings of alienation and "not fitting in."

name: internet
description: The internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks that has become a defining part of the Information Age—especially in regards to consumer-oriented services like social media, email, and the World Wide Web.

name: introspective
description: Introspective themes contain an analysis of one's own thoughts and feelings, or are a form of interior monologue.

name: regret
description: Themes of regret dwell on past mistakes, negative situations, and missed opportunities in one's life; one reminisces about how things could have been done differently.

name: police
description: Music about the police focuses on law enforcement officers as well as protest against them. The police are a civilian body of people charged with enforcing the law, maintaining public order, and ensuring safety through the legitimate use of force conferred by the state.

name: leisure
description: Leisure covers the activities done in one's free time, ranging from rest and relaxation to pursuing hobbies and other fun experiences.

name: LGBTQ
description: LGBTQ+ themes revolve around people and events within the LGBTQ+ community. Such themes tend to focus on topics surrounding their sexuality and/or gender identity as well as sociopolitical commentary and introspection on those subjects.

name: bisexual
description: Bisexuality is a sexual orientation that refers to attraction to both males and females. The term bisexuality may alternatively be defined as attraction to more than one gender or any gender.

name: gay
description: Gay themes involve men who are attracted to other men and the experiences they share relating to their attraction, such as romantic and sexual relationships. This can include bisexual or otherwise queer men, as well as any men or male-leaning nonbinary people who identify with the term.

name: lesbian
description: Lesbian themes involve women who are attracted to other women and the experiences that relate to their attraction, such as sexual and romantic relationships. This may include homosexual, bisexual or otherwise queer women, as well as any woman or nonbinary person who identifies with the term. Lesbian themes may also encompass sociopolitical commentary and movements relevant to lesbianism and lesbian rights, including lesbian-identified feminist movements centering women and female friendship, such as political lesbianism.

name: literature
description: Music with lyrics about written works or authors, including activities like reading and writing literary works. Music can incorporate themes of literature by basing a narrative around an existing literary work.

name: Biblical
description: Music that evokes themes, imagery, and stories from the Bible, including examples such as the stories found in the Tanakh (such as the creation narratives and the exodus of the Israelites detailed in the Torah) and the Christian New Testament (the concept of salvation in the Gospel and apocalyptic themes in Revelation).

name: comics
full_path: theme > literature > comics | theme > visual arts > comics
description: Music about or inspired by comics includes their characters, creators, and storytelling techniques. It may include references to specific heroes, villains, franchises, or even drawing styles used in comics.

name: love
description: Love songs relate to themes of romance and falling in love but also cover heartbreak and breakup. When optimistic, they are generally romantic and/or passionate.

name: breakup
description: Breakup themes relate to lost love, divorce, and other forms of separation within a romantic setting.

name: loyalty
description: Themes of loyalty express firm and unchanging commitment to a person, group or cause, displayed through actions and decisions, even when faced with challenges and difficulties.

name: macabre
description: Macabre lyrical themes express an abnormal interest in disturbing and unpleasant subjects such as death, usually while incorporating graphic imagery. The expression of these themes can vary greatly, ranging from serious and dark settings seeking to disturb the listener to ironic or even humorous contexts, sometimes serving as a juxtaposition to upbeat music.

name: gore
full_path: theme > macabre > gore | theme > violence > gore
description: Gore-themed music focuses on extreme violence and bloodshed. It focuses on portraying gory imagery with over-the-top gruesome descriptions of violence against the human body, such as mutilation, decapitation, and decomposition, sometimes while incorporating the use of medical terminology and pathological diseases for increased shock value. Gory imagery is often attributed to Metal genres such as Death Metal, as well as Hip Hop artists within the Horrorcore genre, with many bands and artists in these style taking lyrical influences from Slasher films and Sadistic Horror. Death metal bands that pioneered this aesthetic also went on to inspire more extreme metal subgenres, such as Goregrind, in which gore-themed music became more exclusive to their respective genres.

name: maritime
description: Music with a maritime theme focuses on navigation and commerce on or bordering a sea as well as traveling over a sea and involves ships, boats, harbours, quays, docks, sailors, seafaring, seaports.

name: marriage
description: Artists may discuss a variety of marital themes, such as proposals, engagements, weddings, divorces, elopement, and general, day-to-day married life. Some artists may cater particular songs, albums, or playlists to serve the particular tone of a wedding context.

name: divorce
description: Divorces often include reorganizing the duties and responsibilities of the partners within the marriage. Often sanctioned by a court or another legal authority, matters can include alimony, distribution of property, and the division of debt or other assets. Children can also be significantly impacted by disunion of their parents' marriage, with matters regarding child support and the right of custody playing a major role. This differs from the annulment (cancellation) of a marriage or the partners being legally separated by living apart. Divorce laws can differ based on social attitudes and religious beliefs found throughout the world.

name: exile
description: The theme of exile focuses on forced removal from one's homeland, often due to political or religious persecution, government dictatorship and state repression, or war, often accompanied by nostalgia for the place one left behind and a longing to return.

name: monarchy
description: Music with a monarchy theme focuses on the form of government in which state authority is concentrated in hereditary royalty, typically a king or a queen. Monarchy has historically been a dominant form of government, and monarchs continue to exist with various degrees of authority throughout the world.

name: money
description: Money themes relate to currency or other mediums of economic exchange, mainly focusing on its acquisition or loss. It ranges from lyrics about great financial success to crushing poverty or debt, as well as associated feelings like greed for riches or disillusionment with affluence.

name: gambling
description: Themes of gambling refer to the act of taking risky action in the hope of a desired result, like a prize. Examples of gambling are card games like poker and blackjack, roulette, slot machines, dice and craps, and sports betting on horse racing and boxing matches.

name: poverty
description: Themes of poverty relate to the status of lacking sufficient money or resources to meet basic needs such as food, shelter, and clothing. It can include one's work to escape from poverty or how others are affected by it.

name: mythology
description: Mythological themes draw influence from a collection of traditional tales from a particular culture or religion. Those tales are sometimes meant to explain things such as the origin of the world, life and humans, or natural phenomena. Deities, heroes and fantastical creatures are common ingredients.

name: nature
description: Themes of nature relate to the environment, animals, or can be a form of political environmentalism.

name: animals
description: Animals appear as a theme in music as lyrical content about specific pets, animal rights activism, and fauna in general. Animals have appeared in art since prehistory, with many of the most famous prehistoric cave paintings being representations of animals. This is also reflected in traditional music across the world, with animal-themed music existing in Medieval Europe (e.g., Una panthera), appearing in folk songs in the ancient Chinese collection Classic of Poetry, and forming traditions in indigenous American music such as the wo'i bwikam (coyote songs) of the Yaqui people. Later, as popular music developed, animal-themed songs remained popular, ranging from cutesy novelty songs, such as "The Doggie in the Window," to odes about an artist's pet, like "Delilah," or more general songs, including "The Red Rooster." The growth in popularity in the animal rights movement in the second half of the 20th century also led to many political songs tied to the ideology, especially in the Punk / Post-Punk / Hardcore sphere.

name: cats
description: Cats are a broad group of carnivorous mammals. They are known for being quick and intelligent, feeding on small prey like mice and rats, and communicating via growls, grunts, meows, purrs, and/or hisses. While other cats, like lions, cougars, cheetahs, and leopards, are all part of the family, the most common depiction of cats in music is the house cat, known for its signature meows and purrs and being one of the most common pets for humans. Music with cat themes in general can range from adding cat sounds to using cat behaviors as symbolism for traits like warmth, companionship, mysteriousness, and playfulness.

name: dogs
description: Music about dogs features the type of carnivorous mammal known for its signature bark, hunting abilities, strong sense of smell, and assistance to humans. As one of the most common household pets, often nicknamed "man's best friend," they are often represented as loyal companions with the ability to emotionally support and protect humans. Some dogs may also play a role in military and law enforcement and aiding disabled people.

name: pets
description: Pets are domesticated animals kept for companionship rather than for work, agriculture, or research. Two of the most popular species kept as pets are dogs and cats, but many other species are also commonly kept for this purpose.

name: nightlife
description: Themes of nightlife involve entertainment available at nighttime, usually in urban areas. This can include clubs, bars, concerts and other forms of entertainment.

name: nostalgia
description: Themes of lyrical nostalgia revolve around an artist longing for a period in the past.

name: obsession
description: Obsession is a theme about intense focus on a person, idea, or activity in a way that can become detrimental to one's well-being. It can be driven by many emotions but is usually a result of love or fascination.

name: occult
description: Occult themes relate to things which are seen as arcane, hidden, and/or paranormal. These often delve into esoteric spiritual territory.

name: paranoia
description: Themes of paranoia deal with thoughts and feelings of distrust toward others accompanied by persecutory beliefs (thinking that something or someone is out to get oneself), sometimes to the point of irrationality and delusion.

name: paranormal
description: Paranormal events and abilities refer to strange phenomena described in popular and folk culture as beyond normal scientific understanding and thought to involve unusual, unknown forces. These include seeing or hunting ghosts, poltergeists, ufology, cryptozoology, human auras, extrasensory perception, telekinesis, levitation, and other psychic powers, etc. Such paranormal events are often a subject of fringe pseudoscientific research by people who seek to find rational explanations for them. The word paranormal is sometimes used interchangeably with the supernatural, but the latter includes metaphysical and divine aspects of religion as well as fantasy and other fictional settings where phenomena that are beyond the regular laws of nature are nonetheless considered normal within their context.

name: patriotic
description: Patriotic themes deal with patriotism and/or a sense of pride towards one's country or nation.

name: philosophical
description: Philosophical themes deal with the principles of reality, existence, knowledge, and/or values.

name: existential
description: Existential themes in music can range from the thought-provoking and often introspective deconstruction of one's own existence, to a description of a mental breakdown attached to an existential crisis. These themes can also often be linked to a sense of personal freedom, confusion about one's role in the universe, or even rarely extend to nihilistic concepts.

name: nihilistic
description: Nihilistic themes in music cover a set of beliefs that the norms (social, moral, or otherwise) possess no necessity beyond their functional, instrumental use by particular institutions (state, church, etc.). This extends to believing the human life has no inherent meaning, and no intrinsic, metaphysical value.

name: pirates
description: Pirate-themed music tends to use lyrical themes and aesthetics derived from The Golden Age of Piracy. It can be performed traditionally in the style of Sea Shanty or in a more contemporary manner centered around the popular mythology of pirates. Topics tend to include sailing the seas, piracy and robbery, labor work in the ship, and hunting for treasure. Artists also commonly rely on musical elements like accordions, fiddles, theatrical accents, raspy vocals, or pirate-related terms to reinforce common tropes associated with pirates.

name: prison
description: Contains themes of prison, which is a facility where people are incarcerated under the authority of the state, typically as punishment for crimes.

name: radio
description: Music with a radio theme references the system that wirelessly broadcasts sound via electromagnetic waves or the Internet as well as the stations and programs that produce this sound. It could include its influence on culture or the act of tuning in and listening to the radio.

name: science
description: Scientific research and methods, when combined with various fields of study, can help organize and explain information about the physical world.

name: science fiction
description: Sci-fi themes are generally speculative and imaginative narratives about futuristic science and technology, such as time and advanced space travel, and can extend to paranormal subject matter.

name: self-hatred
description: Self-hatred themes refer to the dislike or hatred of oneself, or an anger and prejudice towards oneself and/or a group to which one belongs.

name: self-love
description: Self-love, in its modern connotation, is perceived as an intrinsic and necessary value for human beings to have, especially for one’s own mental health awareness and the support or help thereof.

name: sexual
description: Sexual themes relate to sexual activities, and other similar lustful actions.

name: kink
description: Kink refers to nonstandard sexual preferences and practices and the culture that surrounds them. Common kinks include BDSM and fixation on certain objects, body parts, or types of people. Theming around kinks is common in popular music, particularly in more underground spaces, such as Industrial / Noise music.

name: shamanism
description: Shamanism is a spiritual practice in which a person (shaman) interacts with the spirit world, typically by means of rituals that induce altered states of consciousness such as trance, usually for the communal purpose of healing or divination.

name: sleep
description: Themes of sleep revolve around the activity of sleeping and the need for rest as well as the lack of sleep.

name: dreams
description: The theme dreams depicts the experience of dreaming — the sequence of flowing thoughts, images, and emotions that happens in a person's mind during sleep. Oftentimes, they are represented with surreal or abstract imagery.

name: sports
description: Sport themes relate to the many various physical games played worldwide, and can include barracking of one's favourite team, or just be general lyrics about the games in question.

name: association football
description: Association football, commonly known as football or soccer, is a team sport played between two sides of 11 players each who aim to score by getting the ball into the opposing goal, primarily using their feet. Association football has a longstanding connection to music, including traditional Football Chants, which are sung at games to celebrate the crowd's team or insult an opposing team. Some association football events, like FIFA World Cup, commission artists to create official theme songs with relevant lyrics, such as "Game Time." Occasionally, musicians will record songs for specific teams, such as "Three Lions," which represented England's participation in the 1996 UEFA European Championship tournament.

name: baseball
description: Music about baseball focuses on the bat-and-ball sport played between two teams of nine players who take turns pitching and fielding or batting and running, attempting to score by circling four bases over the course of nine rounds, or innings, of regular play. The game is popular in the Americas and East Asia.

name: boxing
description: Boxing is a combat sport involving two participants fighting using punches. Music relating to boxing can be about topics such as boxers, matches or the act of boxing.

name: racing
description: Racing refers to the sport of engaging in contests of speed, encompassing various subcategories such as foot racing, animal racing, and motorsports.

name: wrestling
description: Wrestling is a grappling-based sport that is performed in many forms, most notably amateur wrestling and predetermined professional wrestling. Music relating to wrestling can be about topics such as wrestlers, matches or the act of wrestling.

name: suburban
description: Music that thematically revolves around any outlying area that surrounds inner cities, especially the lives of either individual people or larger communities within a residential area or neighborhood that can be considered suburban.

name: Sun
description: The Sun is the star the Earth orbits. It plays a central role in human life and so has been a perennial theme in music across time and cultures. Music can evoke the Sun in many ways: as a symbol of joy, renewal, or time; of warm weather or daytime; or as an object of worship or reverence.

name: technology
description: Technology is the application of scientific and conceptual knowledge for practical use, often manifesting in the tools that emerge from such efforts. Lyrics can incoporate themes of technology by focusing on certain technological advancements or discussing humanity's relationship with technology.

name: robots
description: Music with a robots theme references programmable machines that are capable of performing specified tasks. Musical references to these machines are often about their relationships with humans, their capabilities of advanced thought, and their correlation with other forms of technology and artificial intelligence. Due to their futuristic public perception, it has become a very common theme in science fiction.

name: television
description: Music with lyrics about television or television shows. It may include commentary on television's impact on culture, references to television programs, or simply the act of watching television.

name: travel
description: Travel-themed music describes a journey to another place, often mentioning the emotions associated with these trips, such as love for a specific location or homesickness.

name: vehicles
description: A vehicle is a machine that is often used to transport people or goods. Most known types of vehicles include cars, bikes, planes, trains, boats, trucks, buses, and tractors. Lyrics that refer to vehicles might involve personal experiences when driving or riding them, or contain specific references to certain brands or models, mainly as status symbols.

name: cars
description: Cars are road vehicles with four wheels. They are typically meant to seat one to eight people at a time. Cars and driving are often used to symbolize freedom and independence. They can also symbolize status, with street racing and luxury brands being common topics for bragging in songs. Songs can also be based around car infrastructure, such as highways, freeways and resulting traffic. Listening to music while driving in the car is a common pastime, with many songs having been written and mixed explicitly for this purpose.

name: trucks
description: Trucks are heavier motor vehicles intended to transport cargo across large distances or enable specialized work, such as mixing concrete or fighting fires. Trucks vary in terms of size and utility. Pickup trucks are a type often used for passenger transportation, while larger variants like 6x4s are designed to handle large loads. Lyrics about trucks are common in Country, particularly in Truck Driving Country and Bro-Country.

name: video games
description: Music about video games, including games played on consoles, arcade machines, handheld devices, and personal computers. This may include references to specific consoles or brands (e.g., PlayStation, Xbox, or Nintendo), specific games and franchises, or online gaming.

name: violence
description: Music that lyrically discusses or describes violent acts, ranging from physical altercations, murders, and in rare cases domestic violence or sexual assault.

name: visual arts
description: Music with a visual arts theme is about visual art or its creation. Common visual art forms include painting, drawing, comics, sculpture, photography, architecture, ceramics, design, television, and film. Music can either lyrically describe specific works, notable visual artists, the creative process, or the culture of visual art, or it can evoke specific works through instrumental music.

name: anime and manga
full_path: theme > visual arts > anime and manga
description: Anime and manga refer to works produced in Japan, anime being animated works and manga being comics or graphic novels. Both mediums were originally based in illustration but also include other techniques such as computer animation. Japanese franchises like Dragon Ball and Pokémon became hugely popular internationally in the 1990s, and subcultures dedicated to anime and manga have formed across the globe. Anime in particular has become a popular topic in music, from niche fan communities to underground rap to international pop hits.

name: film
description: Music with a film theme is about movies or the art of filmmaking. It may include references to film characters or actors, base lyrical narratives around movie plots, or show appreciation for movies in general.

name: war
description: War themes relate to a state of armed conflict between different nations or states, or between different groups within a nation or state. Songs with war themes are often martial in nature.

name: farming
description: Farming is the cultivation of the soil. It encompasses a range of practices and traditions in the areas of planting, tending, and harvesting, as well as breeding and raising livestock. Farming has taken many forms throughout thousands of years of human history and prehistory, categorized into various forms of shifting cultivation, subsistence farming, and intensive farming. Being a central practice across many human societies, farming has long been a prominent theme in musical traditions up to the present, often in the form of work songs but also associated with other facets of rural life.

name: mining
description: Mining is the extraction of valuable resources from the surface of the earth, often using tools such as pickaxes and drill rigs. Songs about mining typically focus on the hardship, danger, and physical endurance required for the work. Mining songs in the Folk and Work Song genres date back many centuries, with traditional Geordie song "The Collier's Rant" potentially composed around 1650. These songs were popular in mining communities around the UK, in areas such as Cornwall, Wales and Lancashire. Traditional mining songs were also present in South Africa ("Shosholoza"), Canada ("Jolly Wee Miner Men") and Australia ("The Miner"). In the late 20th century, mining songs became more prominent in mainstream music. Songs such as Tennessee Ernie Ford's "Sixteen Tons," Bee Gees's "New York Mining Disaster 1941," and Johnny Cash's version of "Dark as the Dungeon" on At Folsom Prison brought miners' experience to a wider audience. Contemporary Folk artists such as Pete Seeger and Woody Guthrie also wrote many songs about miners and mining disasters, tying them to broader themes about human resilience and labor rights. With the boom in popularity of the game Minecraft in the early 2010s, a wave of parody songs about the topic of mining appeared, with tracks such as "Don't Mine at Night - Minecraft Parody" and "Mine the Diamond (A Minecraft Song)" addressing the subject, albeit in a fictional manner.

name: androgynous vocals
description: Music containing lyrics sung or spoken in an ambiguous or androgynous manner.

name: belting
description: Belting is a vocal technique where a singer carries the heavier, more powerful weight of their chest voice above its natural break, blending it with head resonance to produce a loud, sustained, and emotionally intense sound in the middle to upper registers. Originally developed in early Gospel music and Broadway theaters as a way to project over live instrumentation without a microphone, belting has since become a cornerstone of emotional climaxes in Soul, R&B / Soul / Funk, Rock, and many kinds of Pop music.

name: crooning
description: Crooning is a smooth, intimate vocal style that arose in 1920s Jazz and Traditional Pop as improved microphones allowed singers to explore greater dynamic ranges. This style was most popular from the 1940s to the late 1960s, with Bing Crosby and Frank Sinatra being some of the most well-known crooners.

name: deadpan
description: A deadpan delivery is performed in a dry, expressionless, and matter-of-fact fashion. This sort of delivery can also be used comedically.

name: falsetto
description: Falsetto is a vocal technique occupying frequency ranges above the register of modal voice (the vocal range most commonly used in speech and singing). Falsetto is produced by vibrating the ligamentous edges of the vocal chords. The falsetto register gives vocals a breathy, airy sound while being more limited in tone quality, although vocal training can produce a stronger falsetto sound. Falsetto is widely used across folk, classical, and popular music traditions. The term was historically used to refer exclusively to male singers, and it was formerly believed that only men were capable of producing falsetto, although scientific research has since proven that women also have a falsetto register.

name: female vocalist
description: Music containing lyrics sung or spoken by female vocalists.

name: gang vocals
description: Music with gang vocals contains lyrics sung, spoken, or usually shouted by multiple people at once in a raw and unpolished manner. It is common in Punk / Post-Punk / Hardcore and Hip Hop music and creates a powerful, anthemic sound.

name: harsh vocals
description: Harsh vocals encompass a range of vocal performance techniques including screaming, growling, shrieking, rasping, or a similar dissonant and aggressive sound. They are strongly associated with extreme Metal genres such as Death Metal, though they also appear in other genres such as Punk / Post-Punk / Hardcore and Industrial.

name: gurgling vocals
full_path: vocals > harsh vocals > growling > gurgling vocals
description: Gurgling vocals are extremely low and wet, creating a dense, bubbling sound. They are created when vocalists manipulate their mouth, tongue, throat, and saliva. Gurgling vocals are most often found in genres like Slam Death Metal, Goregrind, and Deathcore.

name: male vocalist
description: Music containing lyrics sung or spoken by male vocalists.

name: murmuring
description: A murmur, mumble, or mutter is a voice that is quiet and difficult to understand, whether because it is far away, sung or spoken as though to oneself, obscured by other sounds in the environment or mix, enunciated poorly, or very low volume. A murmur is sometimes thought of as interchangeable with a whisper, but the latter is an unvoiced mode of phonation that is not necessarily quiet or indistinct.

name: nonbinary vocalist
description: Music containing lyrics sung or spoken by nonbinary vocalists.

name: nonlexical vocables
description: Found in a wide variety of musical traditions around the world, nonlexical vocables are vocally produced sounds without any lexical meaning. Some examples of nonlexical vocables include scat singing, Yodeling, and Beatboxing.

name: scat singing
description: Scat singing is a vocal improvisation style in which singers use nonsensical syllables to mimic instrumental solos. It emerged in the early 20th century from Ragtime traditions and became a defining element of Vocal Jazz, popularized by artists like Louis Armstrong, as exemplified in the song "Heebie Jeebies."

name: pitched-down vocals
description: Pitched-down vocals are commonly used as a stylistic choice in music production to create a deeper or more bassy vocal sound. The technique appears in a wide variety of genres including but not limited to Hip Hop, Chopped and Screwed, Goregrind, and Vaporwave.

name: pitched-up vocals
description: Pitched-up vocals are often used as a stylistic choice to create a robotic, alien, or exaggerated voice. They appear frequently in electronic music genres like Bubblegum Dance, Bubblegum Bass and Hyperpop, with their heavy use of autotune, as well as in Chipmunk Soul, Digicore, Nightcore and even K-Pop/J-Pop.

name: sing-rapping
description: Sing-rapping features rapped vocals with highly melodic elements. It is most commonly found in a Hip Hop context, with Kanye West's album 808s & Heartbreak helping to popularize the style. Rappers like Young Thug and Future have found mainstream success and influence while often using the technique. Sing-rapping also exists outside of a Hip Hop context, albeit less commonly. Singers like Taylor Swift and Ariana Grande have seen mainstream success with the technique on Pop songs.

name: talk-singing
description: Talk-singing, or Sprechgesang, is a technique that incorporates speech-like vocals. Sprechgesang initially referred to the recitative technique found in Opera, but it later came to refer to a vocal technique used in popular music, such as Rock, which emphasizes speech-like sounds rather than melody in singing, similar to the Sprechstimme vocal technique associated with composers from the Second Viennese School, like Arnold Schoenberg. It has also been connected to the vocal technique found in Talking Blues and has drawn comparisons to rapping as well, though talk-singing significantly differs from the latter and does not share its emphasis on rhythm. This technique was first popularized by vocalists such as Lou Reed and Bob Dylan in the 1960s and '70s; it later spread to Post-Punk and Alternative Rock. In the 2010s and '20s, artists from the Windmill Scene also incorporated the technique.

name: throat singing
description: Throat singing involves manipulation of the larynx, tongue, and mouth to create harmonic effects, often delivering the auditory impression of more than one pitch being sung at once.

name: toasting
description: Toasting consists of rhythmic spoken vocals performed by a deejay and is associated with Jamaican sound system culture. The deejay delivers improvised or prepared lines over a track, often using rhyme, repetition, call-and-response, and playful boasts. These vocals were initially only spoken over parts of instrumentals and were not intended for professional recording. However, deejay U-Roy began toasting over full tracks in the late 1960s and early 1970s in a style more suited for studio recording rather than live performance. Toasting helped shape Reggae and Dancehall performances and is considered an important influence on the MC style of many genres, including Hip Hop, UK Garage, and Grime.

name: whispering
description: Whispering is an unvoiced mode of phonation in which the vocal cords are abducted so that they do not vibrate, using the breath but not the voice.

name: yarling
description: Yarling is a deep, guttural vocal style with affected pronunciation, popularized by the Grunge band Pearl Jam's lead singer Eddie Vedder. Yarling came to be found in subsequent popular grunge and Post-Grunge bands like Stone Temple Pilots and Creed; however, the vocal style waned in popularity with the decline of the second wave of post-grunge.
